**Wire verb `genes orthology`**: Build an Ensembl Compara orthology snapshot for a set of species from their gene sets, the gene trees and every species' homology dump, and optionally write it as Parquet and say, gene by gene, how far Compara's inference got in another species.

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `release` (wire `--release`) | `string` | required | — | `an Ensembl release number, e.g. 116` | The Ensembl release of the Compara inputs. Required, never defaulted: the release is part of the answer. mzLib holds the gene trees and every dump to it, but only when their file names carry a release (Compara.116.protein\_default.homologies.tsv.gz, vertebrates.GeneTree\_content.default.e116.txt.gz); a renamed file is not checked, and the result's caveats say which. A GTF's own number is not compared with it: Ensembl publishes some species with their own annotation release (Saccharomyces\_cerevisiae.R64-1-1.63.gtf.gz in release 116), so mzLib holds a gene set to the dumps by content instead. |
| `gtfs` (wire `--species`) | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line; each exactly three tab-separated fields` | Read from stdin (not an option), first: one line per species, the species' Ensembl production name (homo\_sapiens, as the dumps' species column spells it), a tab, gtf or gene-set, a tab, and the path. gtf is an Ensembl primary-assembly GTF, plain or .gz, read with EnsemblGeneSet.LoadGtf; gene-set is the compact table mzLib's EnsemblGeneSetWriter makes from one, read with EnsemblGeneSetReader.Load, which keeps the GTF's provenance. These lines are the snapshot's species. A species listed twice, a kind other than gtf or gene-set, or a missing file is a usage error. Blank lines are skipped. |
| `dumps` (wire `--dumps`) | `string[]` | required | — | `exactly one per species` | Read from stdin (not an option), after a line holding only --: one Compara homology dump path per line (homologies/SPECIES/Compara.RELEASE.protein\_default.homologies.tsv.gz, plain or .gz), each read with ComparaHomologyDump.Load for every species given. The dump's genome is read from its rows, not its name. mzLib requires EVERY species' dump: Compara puts each of a pair's relationships in one of the pair's two dumps, arbitrarily, so a missing dump would silently lose them. A missing dump, two of one species, or one of a species not given is mzLib's refusal, a usage error. |
| `gene_trees` (wire `--gene-trees`) | `path` | required | — | — | Compara's gene-tree membership dump, COLLECTION.GeneTree\_content.default.eRELEASE.txt.gz (plain or .gz), read with ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load. It is what tells a gene whose tree holds no gene of the other species from one whose tree does but got no ortholog call. |
| `restrict_gene_trees` (wire `--restrict-gene-trees`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Keep only the gene-tree members in the given gene sets (ComparaGeneTreeContent.Load with restrictTo, the gene sets). Absent: mzLib's default, restrictTo null, which keeps every gene in the file, 4.2 million for the vertebrate collection of release 116 (mzLib's ComparaGeneTreeContent remarks). The snapshot, its id and every written byte are the same either way; only memory, gene\_trees.member\_count and gene\_trees.restricted\_to\_gene\_sets differ. mzLib checks the one-tree and one-canonical-protein rules only on the genes kept. |
| `out` (wire `--out`) | `path` | absent | — | `a directory that does not exist or is empty` | Write the snapshot to this directory with OrthologySnapshotWriter.WriteAsync: Parquet tables (zstd) genes/SPECIES.parquet, members/SPECIES.parquet and pairs/A\_\_B.parquet, plus views.sql (DuckDB table macros) and manifest.json. The directory and its subfolders are created. A DIRECTORY, not a .tsv file: the PYB-1 extension rule is for options that write one table. mzLib refuses a directory that is not empty, because a snapshot is written once and compared with a later one, never updated in place; the bridge applies that same refusal, and refuses a path that is a file, before any input is read. Absent: nothing is written. |
| `pair_status` (wire `--pair-status`) | `string` | absent | — | `FROM,TO: two different species of the snapshot` | Return pair\_status: every gene of FROM's gene set, in ordinal order of gene id, with its status in TO (OrthologySnapshot.PairStatus). Two production names separated by a comma, e.g. homo\_sapiens,mus\_musculus. Both must be species given on stdin, and different; the bridge checks that before any input is read, with the rule mzLib's PairStatus applies. One direction per call: status is not symmetric. Absent: pair\_status is null. |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | --release or --gene-trees missing or given without a value; --out or --pair-status given without a value; a value after --restrict-gene-trees |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | no species lines on stdin, no line holding only --, or no dump paths after it; a species line that is not species, tab, gtf or gene-set, tab, path; a species listed twice |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | a GTF, gene-set table, dump or gene-trees file that does not exist; --out naming a file or a directory that is not empty (OrthologySnapshotWriter.WriteAsync's refusal, applied before any input is read) |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | --pair-status not two comma-separated names, naming a species not given on stdin, or one species twice (the rule of OrthologySnapshot.PairStatus, applied before any input is read) |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | mzLib's OrthologySnapshot.Build refused the inputs as not fitting together (ArgumentException, with mzLib's message): the gene trees or a dump name a release other than --release; a dump is of a species not given, two dumps are of one species, or a species has no dump |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | a file mzLib's reader refuses (InvalidDataException, naming file and line): a GTF gene row without gene\_id; a table that is not a gene-set table; a dump with other columns, a short row, a value that is not a number, an unknown homology\_type, a paralog between two species, an ortholog within one, or a second genome; a gene-tree row without four cells or with a flag other than Y or N, or a kept gene in two trees or without exactly one canonical protein |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | OrthologySnapshot.Build found data that breaks the snapshot's rules (InvalidDataException): one gene in two species' gene sets, a homology naming a gene its species' gene set lacks (the gene set and the dumps are from different releases), or one homology id with two different rows |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | the snapshot could not be written (IOException from the disk) |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- Every species' homology dump is required, and mzLib refuses a call without one. Compara's README warns that each genome's dump holds an arbitrary subset of its relationships, and in practice they partition: in release 116 every human-mouse orthology is in the mouse dump and none is in the human one, so the dump named after one species gives a complete-looking, badly incomplete answer.
- Orthology is asserted per species pair and is not transitive: A~B and B~C do not make A~C. Never chain pairs into groups. The written views.sql's species\_set3 macro, and mzLib's OrthologySnapshot.SpeciesSet, form a tuple only when every two members are orthologs.
- Nothing is picked, merged or collapsed: a one-to-many or many-to-many orthology is several rows, and a gene's paralogs are the pair (s, s).
- A status says how far Compara's inference got, not what biology holds. no\_edge\_in\_shared\_tree is the nearest the data comes to no ortholog exists; tree\_lacks\_target\_species and not\_in\_any\_tree mean nothing was compared.
- Every biotype is in pair\_status and in genes/SPECIES.parquet. Which genes form a denominator is the caller's choice: filter on gene\_biotype. mzLib's own human-to-mouse check counted protein-coding plus IG and TR genes, which is not the same set as protein\_coding alone.
- Values are Compara's, verbatim: a NULL in a dump stays null in the Parquet (identity, dn, ds, goc\_score, wga\_coverage, is\_high\_confidence), never 0 or false. identity\_a and identity\_b differ because each is over its own protein.
- The gene set and the dumps must be from one release: mzLib refuses a homology whose gene is not in its species' gene set. Use the primary-assembly GTF (Species.Assembly.Release.gtf.gz), as for genes resolve.
- A snapshot is written once. The same inputs give the same bytes and the same snapshot\_id, so a later release is a new directory compared with the old one; a directory that is not empty is refused, never overwritten.
- mzLib ships a writer and no reader. Query the Parquet with DuckDB (load views.sql for the orthologs, pair\_status and species\_set3 macros), pyarrow, polars or R's arrow.
- Ensembl names every species' dump Compara.RELEASE.protein\_default.homologies.tsv.gz in its own folder, and the pairs tables' source\_dump column records only the file name, so it cannot tell two species' dumps apart. manifest.json's inputs list each dump with its species and sha256.
